faq.q: What does the Analyse button actually report?
faq.a: It scans the query with regex and lists the tables referenced (from FROM, JOIN, UPDATE, INTO, DELETE FROM), the columns in the first SELECT, and which join types appear. It flags SELECT * as a performance warning and flags an UPDATE or DELETE with no WHERE clause as a red error since those hit every row. It also rates complexity Low/Moderate/High by counting subqueries and joins.

faq.q: Does the dialect setting change how my SQL is formatted?
faq.a: No. The MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, and Oracle options only display a reference note about that dialect's quoting and syntax, for example backticks in MySQL, brackets in SQL Server, and TOP n versus LIMIT. The actual indentation, keyword casing, and line breaking are the same across dialects. The tokenizer does preserve backtick and bracket-quoted identifiers as-is.

faq.q: What validation errors will stop formatting?
faq.a: Before formatting it checks for unbalanced parentheses and unclosed string literals; either is treated as a fatal error, so the output shows your raw query unchanged with the error displayed. A SELECT with no FROM clause raises a yellow warning but still formats. These checks come from the same tokenizer used for formatting, so comments and strings are handled correctly.

faq.q: How does Minify differ from Format, and does it change my data?
faq.a: Minify collapses the query to a single line, removing all comments and extra whitespace while still applying your chosen keyword case. Format instead breaks clauses like SELECT, FROM, WHERE, and each JOIN onto their own lines with your indent setting. Both run entirely in your browser; your input, settings, and last query are saved to local storage under sqlFormatterV2.
